evidence.note: Rather than relying on RL to spontaneously and unpredictably produce advanced reasoning behaviors (the 'aha moment'), this paper explicitly trains three separate specialists on synthetic, self-verifiable deduction/induction/abduction tasks (Peirce's classical inference triad), merges them via linear parameter-space interpolation, and shows this meta-ability-aligned checkpoint both generalizes zero-shot to seven unseen math/coding/science benchmarks and raises the attainable performance ceiling of subsequent domain-specific RL by ~2-4% over an instruction-tuned baseline at both 7B and 32B scale.
evidence.title: Beyond ’Aha!’: Toward Systematic Meta-Abilities Alignment in Large Reasoning Models
